motions.item_title: Appoint Mary Hammond to the Senior Citizens Advisory Council, completing a 4-year term through…
motions.motion: Councilmember Clark moved to appoint Mary Hammond to the Senior Citizens Advisory Council, completing a 4-year term through 2025. Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Mary Hammond joins senior advisory council
motions.summary: The council appointed Mary Hammond to the Senior Citizens Advisory Council, completing a four-year term that runs through 2025.
motions.impact: Nothing changes for residents — this fills a volunteer seat on the board that advises the city on issues affecting seniors.

motions.motion: Councilmember Burnham moved to approve the Consent Agenda, removing items 12.G. and 12.H. from the agenda. Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Consent agenda approved, two items pulled
motions.summary: The council approved its consent agenda — the bundle of uncontested items — after pulling two of the items off it.
motions.impact: Nothing changes for residents on its own. This is the batch vote the council uses to clear routine business in one step.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Adjusting the Boundary Line of Certain Real Property from the Geographical Boundaries of the Town of Cedar Fort to the Geographical Boundaries of Eagle Mountain City
motions.motion: Councilmember Burnham moved to approve an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Adjusting the Boundary Line of Certain Real Property from the Geographical Boundaries of the Town of Cedar Fort to the Geographical Boundaries of Eagle Mountain City. Councilmember Clark seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Land moved from Cedar Fort into Eagle Mountain
motions.summary: The council moved a piece of property out of the Town of Cedar Fort and into Eagle Mountain's city boundaries.
motions.impact: If you own or live on that land, Eagle Mountain now provides your city services and sets your taxes and zoning rules instead of Cedar Fort. The motion doesn't identify the property.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Section 17.10.030 Definitions
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to approve an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Section 17.10.030 Definitions. Councilmember Clark seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Zoning definitions updated
motions.summary: The council updated the definitions section of the city's land use code; the motion does not say which terms were changed.
motions.impact: Nothing changes day to day. Definitions set the meaning of terms used elsewhere in the zoning code, and matter mainly to developers and the staff applying those rules.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapters 8.07 Nuisance Abatement and 8.15 Noise.
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to approve an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapters 8.07 Nuisance Abatement and 8.15 Noise. Councilmember Burnham seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Noise and property nuisance rules rewritten
motions.summary: The council approved changes to the city's nuisance abatement and noise rules, though the motion itself does not spell out what was changed.
motions.impact: These are the rules behind noise complaints and property-upkeep enforcement, so they apply citywide. The motion text doesn't say what changed — read the ordinance before assuming your yard or late-night habits are affected.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Establishing a Mortgage Assistance Program.
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to approve a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Adopting a Mortgage Assistance Program with the following changes: 1. Amend the maximum loan amount to $25,000; 2. Amend to indicate there is no maximum to the applicant(s)’ cash contribution to the purchase of a property; 3. Amend to indicate there is no minimum or maximum to the applicant(s)’ liquid assets at closing; 4. Amend the maximum Area Median Income to $151,800 for households of 6 or more; 5. Amend the application prioritization and schedule as presented: Namely to reflect prioritization by applicant employment type then prioritization by income relative to area median income with lower income households receiving higher priority; 6. Extend the requirement to respond to applicants regarding minimum qualifications to 15 business days after the application collection period; 7. Remove real estate brokerage fees from the list of eligible closing costs; 8. Direct administration to outsource the eligibility review process; and 9. Direct staff to edit the draft policy documents to reflect these amendments. Councilmember Clark seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Mortgage help: city loans up to $25,000
motions.summary: The city created a mortgage assistance program offering homebuyers loans of up to $25,000, prioritized by job type and then by lower household income.
motions.impact: If you're buying a home in Eagle Mountain, you can apply for up to $25,000 toward the purchase. Households of six or more earning up to $151,800 may qualify, and an outside reviewer will check eligibility.
